post.description: The signature is checked through the gateway (400 `PAYMENT_SIGNATURE_INVALID`, also for another order’s result). The browser’s result alone is not final: a valid one makes the payment `PENDING` at most. The server then asks the gateway for the payment itself and applies what the gateway reports, as its notice would: `SUCCEEDED` (captured) or `FAILED` in this answer. Otherwise (capture still to come, gateway unreachable) it stays `PENDING` until the gateway’s notice or the status sweep, so poll the booking’s `paymentStatus`. While the payment is `PENDING` the booking’s hold on the aircraft is kept (48 hours from the order at most, never past the trip). Repeating it changes nothing more.

For the payment gateway only. The signature over the exact body is verified before anything else, and a refused call is stored nowhere; `:provider` is the configured gateway (`mock` in this build). A verified event is stored once (unique per provider event ID) and applied in the same transaction before the 200: a repeated delivery is acknowledged and changes nothing, except that a notice stored before its order was known is applied when it is delivered again. Outcomes only move a payment forward (a failure after a success is ignored); a success changes the booking’s `paymentStatus`, and its status only through the confirmation rule (`CONFIRMED` once the operator’s acceptance, the confirmed price and the payment due are all in; a payment alone never confirms); a success for a closed or already-paid booking is recorded and flagged for operations. A second capture with another gateway payment ID on a paid order is flagged for operations (`DUPLICATE_CAPTURE`). An event for an unknown order is stored and acknowledged (never a 5xx); a status sweep asks the gateway about payments still open after 15 minutes. Limited per address (120 a minute by default, `RATE_LIMIT_WEBHOOK_PER_MINUTE`; 429 `RATE_LIMITED`).

post.description: For accounts without a password (registered with a mobile number), or as an alternative to it. The code goes to the mobile number, or to the email address when there is none. Send the answer’s `verificationId` with the code to `POST /me/erasure`. The code works only there: `POST /auth/otp/verify` refuses it, and `POST /me/erasure` refuses a sign-in code.
post.summary: Send a code to confirm erasing your account

post.description: Irreversible. Confirmed with the current password, or with `verificationId` and `code` from `POST /me/erasure/code`. Your name, contact details, password, saved passengers, sign-ins, notifications and the personal details on past bookings and air ambulance requests (passengers, special requests, contacts, medical details and documents) are erased at once. Booking references, amounts, payments and settlements are kept for the legal and financial record, as are the records of the consents you gave (with the address they were given from) and the audit log (with the address of each action). Messages in a booking’s timeline stay, encrypted, because the timeline cannot be edited. Every sign-in ends; the email address or mobile number can be registered again. 409 `USER_ERASURE_BLOCKED` while something is still open, with one `details` entry per reason (`OPEN_BOOKINGS`, `PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS`, `REFUND_IN_PROGRESS`, `REFUND_DUE`, `PAYMENT_UNDER_REVIEW` (a payment flagged `AMOUNT_MISMATCH` or `DUPLICATE_CAPTURE`), `BALANCE_DUE`, `OPEN_AIR_AMBULANCE`, `RECENT_ACTIVITY`); 401 `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS` for a wrong password; 400 `AUTH_OTP_INVALID` or `AUTH_OTP_EXPIRED` for a wrong or used code; 503 `USER_ERASURE_BUSY` when the account was busy (a lock not free within 5 s, or the erasure not done within 30 s): nothing was erased, send it again (a code is used up, so ask for a new one).

post.description: For an erasure request received another way (email, letter). Customer accounts only. Irreversible; needs a reason and is audited as `user.erase` with counts only. The same data is erased and kept as for `POST /me/erasure`, and the same 409 `USER_ERASURE_BLOCKED` applies. 409 `USER_INVALID_TRANSITION` for an internal staff or operator account, or one already erased. 503 `USER_ERASURE_BUSY` when the account was busy: nothing was erased, send it again.

info.description:
Aviation booking platform API. Conventions: docs/api/api-design.md.

**Envelope.** Every success is `{ data, meta }` (schema `EnvelopeDto`): each route below documents only its `data`. `meta` (`ResponseMetaDto`) holds `requestId`, and on list routes `page`, `pageSize` and `total`; a list route documented as an array answers with that array in `data`.

**Errors.** Every error is `{ error: { code, message, details, requestId } }` (schema `ErrorEnvelopeDto`), with the HTTP status; clients switch on `code`.

refundRate.description: Completed refunds started in the period, per amount collected on payments started in the period.

attempts.description: Payment attempts started in the period.

successRate.description: Succeeded per finished attempt (succeeded or failed). A share from 0 to 1, rounded to 4 decimals; null when there is nothing to divide by.

collected.description: The amount of the succeeded attempts.

flagged.description: Attempts flagged for operations to look at.

requests.description: Booking requests made to it in the period.

responded.description: Requests its staff answered (accepted, rejected or quoted).

responseRate.description: Responded per request. A share from 0 to 1, rounded to 4 decimals; null when there is nothing to divide by.

averageResponseMinutes.description: Whole minutes from the request to its first answer.

declined.description: `OPERATOR_UNAVAILABLE`: the aircraft could not fly although the calendar offered it.

declineRate.description: Declined per request, a measure of availability accuracy (lower is better). A share from 0 to 1, rounded to 4 decimals; null when there is nothing to divide by.

operators.description: Operators with requests in the period, most requests first.

published.description: Those offers that were ever published.

bookingRate.description: Booked per published offer. A share from 0 to 1, rounded to 4 decimals; null when there is nothing to divide by.

open.description: Not yet completed, declined or cancelled.

quoted.description: Those that were sent a quotation.

confirmed.description: Those that were confirmed by operations.

averageMinutesToQuote.description: Whole minutes from the request to its quotation.

averageMinutesToConfirm.description: Whole minutes from the request to its confirmation.

fulfilmentRate.description: Completed per closed request (completed, declined or cancelled). A share from 0 to 1, rounded to 4 decimals; null when there is nothing to divide by.

password.description: The current password. Send this, or verificationId and code.

reason.description: Why the personal data is being erased, for example how the request arrived. Audited and kept: never include the person’s name or contact details.

data.description: The route's documented response: an object, or an array on list routes. `null` when the route returns nothing.

code.description: Stable upper snake case code; clients switch on it, never on `message`.
